Held-out TDD contract cards (orchestrator-owned):

1) retry convergence — authoritative contract: shipped five-attempt workflow loop + ticket AC1; precondition: local HEAD ahead while a deterministic real competitor advances origin before each of the first five push attempts; production path: push_tickets_branch against real temporary refs; tier: integration/real git because reachability and data-loss are the mechanism; postcondition: exactly six pushes, remote HEAD equals local HEAD, both local and all competitor commits remain ancestors; negative control: success before exhaustion performs no terminal push; gate: make test.

2) strict failure matrix — authoritative contract: AC2/4/5; precondition: semantic fault seam selects each real early-return/terminal branch; production path: push_tickets_branch(strict=True); tier: in-process unit with real state where count/reachability matters; postcondition: catchable PushDeliveryError with pinned reason/detail/unpushed count, no sys.exit/stream write; collateral: HEAD/worktree/event set unchanged; paired best-effort call returns None; gate: make test.

3) process boundary — authoritative contract: AC3/7; precondition: real local policy-rejecting origin and one unpushed commit; production path: python -m rebar._store.push push --tracker ... --strict; tier: subprocess; postcondition: nonzero stderr includes reason/detail/count, commit remains reachable, no event/BRIDGE_ALERT file; gate: make test.

4) caller continuity — authoritative contract: AC6; precondition: each semantic caller reaches its shipped push seam; tier: in-process contract tests because call argument/default is the contract; postcondition: event append, batch append, import, close, two delete paths, two compact paths, and claim omit strict or reach strict=False and retain legacy result/disposition.

Surface parity: private module CLI=in scope via subprocess; MCP/API tools=out of strict scope because no new strict surface and existing operations stay best-effort (covered through shared core callers); library facade=existing public operations in scope for continuity, direct strict remains private; automated callers=in scope via full inventory; dual-direction=inbound pull/reconcile out of scope because this leaf changes outbound delivery only. No bespoke concurrency harness: convergence extends the existing shared two-clone regression suite.

compiled_state.description:
## Context

Make `src/rebar/_store/push.py` the authoritative CAS retry implementation before any workflow migrates. The current core stops after three merge attempts and discards the clean merge produced on its final iteration; `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` is the exact shipped source of truth being collapsed: its `max_retries=5` loop performs five push→fetch→merge cycles and the terminal block performs one final `git push origin HEAD:tickets`. `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` independently carries a five-attempt push loop, confirming that five is the existing workflow budget rather than a new threshold. The core is also intentionally best-effort, while the reconciler's ephemeral commit-back requires an opt-in fail-loud disposition.

## Approach

- Extend `push_tickets_branch(base_path, *, strict=False)`; preserve the default for every existing caller.
- Preserve the shipped push-first loop shape exactly: up to five in-loop attempts each perform push first; only a retriable non-fast-forward rejection triggers fetch+merge, followed by an immediate re-push on the next iteration with no backoff. If the fifth in-loop push is rejected and its fetch+merge succeeds, perform exactly one terminal sixth push to spend that clean merged HEAD. An earlier successful push exits with no terminal push.
- Define one reusable `PushDeliveryError` carrying a distinct reason plus `N unpushed commits on <remote>/<branch>..HEAD`. Every strict CORE branch raises it; core never calls `sys.exit` or writes process streams.
- Pin the machine-stable reason vocabulary by branch: `push-disabled`, `async-delivery-unobservable`, `invalid-destination`, `remote-not-found`, `push-policy-declined`, `push-transport-failed`, `merge-recovery-blocked`, `store-epoch-pre-merge`, `store-epoch-during-recovery`, `final-push-rejected`, and `lock-timeout`. The exception/string also carries the underlying git/config detail and unpushed count; tests assert the stable reason value rather than incidental prose.
- Cover terminal non-fast-forward exclusions by preserving their operational class: `_POLICY_DECLINE_MARKERS` map to `push-policy-declined`, while timeouts/network/other transport failures map to `push-transport-failed`; also cover the rebase/merge-recovery guard, both store-epoch guards, final-push exhaustion, lock timeout, `sync.push=off`, `sync.push=async`, malformed destination config, and a missing configured remote.
- Preserve warning-and-return behavior byte-for-byte for the paired best-effort paths.
- Add a parametrized caller-contract proof over the complete current inventory: event append, batch append, NDJSON import, transition close, both delete paths, both compact paths, and claim. Invoke each caller through its existing seam and assert it omits strict delivery (or reaches the shared core with `strict=False`) while retaining its existing return/disposition contract.
- Emit no ticket event and do not resurrect `BRIDGE_ALERT`.
- Keep `push_tickets_branch` push-only; dirty-tree staging/commit belongs to the dependent child. Add the dependency-first private adapter action `python -m rebar._store.push push --tracker ... [--strict]`; this is the sole boundary that catches `PushDeliveryError`, prints its message to stderr, and returns nonzero. Child 2bc9 extends the same adapter with `commit-and-push`.
- Update concurrency documentation to distinguish default best effort from opt-in strict delivery.

## Testing

Use real temporary git repositories for convergence and rejection, in-process fault injection at the actual guard/lock seams for the strict/best-effort branch matrix, and the existing real epoch fixtures for both epoch sites.

RED-first oracle:
- a deterministic competitor wins the first five push-first attempts; current core exhausts three attempts, while the intended loop performs exactly one terminal sixth push that succeeds and makes remote/local convergence GREEN. The oracle pins six total pushes in this full-contention case and no terminal push after any earlier success;
- strict policy rejection and strict transport timeout/failure must both exit nonzero with the exact git detail and escalating unpushed count, but expose distinct stable reasons (`push-policy-declined` versus `push-transport-failed`); no new event file is written; current code returns;
- every strict branch has a paired best-effort control; core tests assert the catchable exception and a real module-CLI subprocess test separately asserts stderr/nonzero translation; semantic fault seams select branches, never source line numbers;
- a parametrized caller-contract test executes the full semantic-plus-string inventory (event append, batch append, NDJSON import, transition close, both delete paths, both compact paths, and claim) through injected call seams and proves every legacy caller still selects best effort while inheriting the shared five-cycle/final-push correction;
- large rejection stderr is classified by the Python core rather than YAML extraction;
- mutation removes the single final push and makes the contention oracle RED; a second-final-push mutation also fails the exact push-count oracle; warn-and-return mutation makes the strict matrix RED.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The push-first loop converges after five deterministic competing pushes: five in-loop pushes are each followed by fetch+merge only on retriable rejection, then exactly one terminal sixth push spends the fifth clean merge. The oracle pins six total pushes in that case, pins no terminal push after earlier success, introduces no duplicate final push, and selects semantic branches without navigating by source line number.
- [x] Every strict core failure branch raises the reusable catchable `PushDeliveryError`; core never calls `sys.exit`, and paired core-boundary tests assert the pinned reason vocabulary (`push-disabled`, `async-delivery-unobservable`, `invalid-destination`, `remote-not-found`, `push-policy-declined`, `push-transport-failed`, `merge-recovery-blocked`, `store-epoch-pre-merge`, `store-epoch-during-recovery`, `final-push-rejected`, `lock-timeout`) and unpushed count.
- [x] The private module `push` action is the sole process boundary translating `PushDeliveryError` to nonzero plus stderr, proven by a real subprocess test; dependent child 2bc9 reuses and extends this adapter.
- [x] Strict `off`, `async`, malformed destination, and missing remote configurations fail explicitly.
- [x] Every paired best-effort case returns normally and preserves local commits and working-tree state.
- [x] A parametrized caller-contract test covers event append, batch append, NDJSON import, transition close, both delete paths, both compact paths, and claim; every site omits strict delivery (or reaches core with `strict=False`), preserves its legacy best-effort return/disposition contract, and inherits only the five-cycle plus exactly-one-final-push durability correction.
- [x] Strict failure writes no ticket event and never emits `BRIDGE_ALERT`.
- [x] Direct `push_tickets_branch` remains push-only.
- [x] Existing narrow-refspec, stash/pop, epoch-guard, and rejection-classification contracts remain green.
- [x] `docs/concurrency.md` distinguishes the unchanged default best-effort contract from opt-in strict delivery, documents the pinned `PushDeliveryError` reason vocabulary (including policy-decline versus transport-failure), and states that all existing callers remain best-effort while inheriting only the five-attempt plus terminal-push durability correction.
- [x] Focused pytest nodes, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `make test` pass.

## Compatibility and rollback

`strict` is keyword-only and defaults false, so existing CLI, MCP, library, importer, and store-write callers retain their contract. No persisted schema changes. This prerequisite lands unused and can be reverted safely before the dependent workflow cutover.
